# National Geographic

> > National Geographic's exploration and science journalism covering wildlife photography, space discoveries, archaeology, and environmental science from around the world.

This collection showcases National Geographic's multimedia storytelling, featuring curated photography from contributors like Steve Winter and Pete Muller, alongside breaking science news from NASA missions, archaeological discoveries, and environmental research. The content spans wildlife documentation in regions like Brazil's Pantanal and Botswana, space exploration including exoplanet discoveries and Hubble imagery, and historical expeditions from Jacques Cousteau to Roald Amundsen.

## Key Topics

- Wildlife photography
- Space exploration and astronomy
- Archaeological discoveries
- Exoplanets and habitable zones
- National Geographic photographers
- NASA missions and Hubble telescope
- Ancient civilizations and artifacts
- Environmental science
- Photo curation and Instagram features
- Jaguars and Pantanal ecosystem
- Polar exploration
- Maya civilization
- Ocean exploration
- Climate and weather patterns
- Kuiper belt and dwarf planets

## Space and Astronomy

- [Hubble Telescope at 20: NASA Astronomers' Top Photos](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100424-hubble-telescope-20th-anniversary-pictures): NASA astronomers select top Hubble telescope photos for 20th anniversary
- [Our Solar System May Have Millions of Twins](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100108-solar-systems-like-ours-twins): Survey reveals Milky Way may host millions of habitable Earthlike planets
- [New Planet System May Be Most Populated Yet Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/101130-new-planets-found-solar-system-twin-science-space): HD 10180 star system may host seven planets, matching our solar system
- [Three New "Plutos"? Possible Dwarf Planets Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/110811-three-new-dwarf-planets-pluto-kuiper-belt-space-science): Three potential dwarf planets discovered in Kuiper belt beyond Neptune
- ["Suicide" Comet Storm Hits Sun—Bigger Sun-Kisser Coming?](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/110117-comets-storm-sun-soho-nasa-sungrazing-science-space): SOHO captures sungrazing comet swarm possibly heralding larger visitor

## Archaeology and Ancient Civilizations

- [Pictures: Odd Maya Tomb Yields Jeweled Teeth, More](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100721-maya-tomb-human-fingers-king-guatemala-science-pictures): Maya royal tomb at El Zotz, Guatemala reveals sacrifice and burial rituals
- [Pictures: Pagan-Cult Worship Objects Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100616-israel-pagan-cult-tomb-objects-pictures): Bronze Age ritual objects discovered at Tel Qashish, Israel excavation
- [Pocahontas's Wedding Chapel Found at Jamestown](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/101110-pocahontas-wedding-chapel-jamestown-science): Church where Pocahontas married John Rolfe discovered in Virginia

## Exploration and Expeditions

- [Jacques Cousteau Centennial: What He Did, Why He Matters](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100611-jacques-cousteau-100th-anniversary-birthday-legacy-google): Jacques Cousteau's centennial tribute highlighting ocean exploration legacy
- [100th Anniversary of Roald Amundsen Reaching South Pole—How the Grueling Race Was Won](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100th-anniversary-of-norwegian-roald-amundsen-reaching-south-polefind-out-how-the-grueling-race-was): Centennial of Amundsen-Scott South Pole race in 1911 Antarctic expedition
- [Video: Giant Undersea Volcano Revealed](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100714-indonesia-okeanos-volcano-exploration-vin-video): First footage of Kawio Barat underwater volcano near Indonesia by NOAA

## Photo Features and Curated Collections

- [Our Favorite Instagram Photos: Jaguar Cubs and Penguin Chicks](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/0909-favorite-instagram): Weekly curated Instagram photos featuring jaguars in Brazil's Pantanal
- [Pictures We Love: Best of October](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/111031-best-news-pictures-lightning-volcano-beluga-bubble): Photo editors' October picks: volcanic lightning, Galápagos tortoise, more
- [Pictures We Love: Best of December](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/111229-best-pictures-month-auroras-deserts-rivers-refugees): December photo highlights from Dhaka, Bangladesh and global news events

## Sports and Environment

- [Vancouver 2010 to Be Warmest Winter Olympics Yet](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100212-vancouver-2010-warmest-winter-olympics): Vancouver 2010 set to be warmest Winter Olympics due to El Niño patterns
- [Did Olympic Athletes Peak in the 1980s?](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100226-vancouver-2010-olympics-new-world-record): Study finds athletic performance approaching human limits at Vancouver 2010
